rationale: Ground truth is essentially an unqualified LGTM with a verification comment confirming boundary validation, unit tests, and L4 regression all passed — X's zero-finding output trivially matches that surface outcome but offers no evidence of actually checking consistency across the four touched files, so it earns no actionability credit. Y independently confirms the same three things the human verifier checked (boundary logic, unit tests, L4 regression) and additionally surfaces a specific, plausible, well-grounded gap — two untouched reliability-suite test files that still hardcode the old '3' lower bound — with exact file/line locations and concrete diffs to apply. Even with some uncertainty about whether those exact files exist as described, the finding is far more substantive and actionable than X's rubber-stamp result.
